newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former US envoy jailed again in HK passports case.
newsitem.headline: Former US envoy jailed again in HK passports case.

text.p: A former top U.S. immigration official was jailed for three months in Hong Kong on Monday for possessing material to make false passports, far less than the 40 months he had received for actually having bogus passports.
Jerry Stuchiner, 45, was sentenced to 40 months in prison last August after he admitted possessing false travel documents.

But the five Honduran passports he was carrying when he was arrested at Hong Kong airport in July were blank except for an official stamp and signature. By legal definition, a travel document must include a photograph.

An appeals court ruled he had been charged with the wrong offence and that his conviction was unsustainable, but officers from the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) rearrested him moments after he left court last month.
This time Stuchiner was charged with the correct offence -- possessing documents for making false instruments -- and was duly sentenced, the ICAC said in a statement on Monday.

The ICAC was working with U.S. Justice Department officials probing a smuggling ring that took illegal migrants from Asia to the United States. Stuchiner at the time of his arrest was the top immigration officer in the U.S. Embassy in Honduras.

Another senior U.S. immigration officer in Hong Kong, John DeBates, was sent back to the United States earlier this year for suspected corruption and abuse of authority. The ICAC is also looking into that case.
